question:
Replace the question mark (?) in the series given below with suitable options.

22, 4, 26, 8, 34, 7, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 41.

GIVEN

• Series: 22, 4, 26, 8, 34, 7, ?

SOLUTION

• Look at the series in groups of "term, added number, result": 22 + 4 = 26; 26 + 8 = 34; 34 + 7 = 41.

• In other words, every alternate term (26, 34, 41) is the sum of the term before it and the small number given after it (4, 8, 7).

• So the missing term is 34 + 7 = 41.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• When a series mixes small and large numbers alternately, test the "add the small number to the previous large number" rule: 22 + 4 = 26, 26 + 8 = 34, 34 + 7 = 41.

NOTE

• Option 1 (42) would need 8 to be added to 34 instead of 7.

• Option 2 (44) would need 10 to be added to 34. ✗

• Option 4 (50) would need 16 to be added to 34. ✗

• Tip: in mixed series, split the odd and even positions or test whether one term is built from the neighbouring terms.

question: Skeleton is to Body as Framework is to ___
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Building.

GIVEN

• Skeleton : Body :: Framework : ?

SOLUTION

• A skeleton is the internal structure that supports and gives shape to the body.

• In the same way, a framework is the structure that supports and gives shape to a building (the steel or concrete frame of a building).

• So the pair is "supporting structure : the thing it supports", and the answer is Building.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Convert the first pair into a sentence: "A skeleton is the supporting structure of a body." Then test: "A framework is the supporting structure of a building" ✓.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Blueprint) is wrong: a blueprint is a plan or design drawing of a structure, not its physical supporting frame.

• Option 2 (Software) is wrong: "software framework" is a technical use of the word, but the question is comparing a physical structure (skeleton–body); a framework is not "the structure of a software" in this analogy in the same direct way, and it is not the best match.

• Option 3 (Machine) is wrong: a machine has a frame or chassis, but "building" is the closest parallel for structure and support.

• Tip: analogy questions are solved by finding the relationship (part–whole, function, cause–effect) and applying it to the second pair.

question: What comes next: 0, 6, 24, 60, 120, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 210.

GIVEN

• Series: 0, 6, 24, 60, 120, ?

SOLUTION

• Each term follows the rule n³ − n = (n − 1) × n × (n + 1), which is the product of three consecutive numbers.

• n = 1: 0 × 1 × 2 = 0; n = 2: 1 × 2 × 3 = 6; n = 3: 2 × 3 × 4 = 24; n = 4: 3 × 4 × 5 = 60; n = 5: 4 × 5 × 6 = 120.

• n = 6: 5 × 6 × 7 = 210 (or 6³ − 6 = 216 − 6 = 210).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• 6 = 1×2×3, 24 = 2×3×4, 60 = 3×4×5, 120 = 4×5×6, so the next is 5×6×7 = 210.

NOTE

• Option 1 (150): does not equal any product of three consecutive numbers (it is 5 × 30). ✗

• Option 2 (180): 5 × 6 × 6 would give 180, which is not three consecutive numbers. ✗

• Option 4 (240): 5 × 6 × 8 would give 240, which is not three consecutive numbers. ✗

• Memorise: n³ − n series: 0, 6, 24, 60, 120, 210, 336, 504.

question: If you are facing north and turn 90° to your right, which direction will you be facing?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. East.

GIVEN

• Initial direction = North. Turn = 90° to the right (clockwise).

SOLUTION

• A right turn means clockwise rotation. The clockwise order of the main directions is North → East → South → West.

• A 90° clockwise turn from North takes you to East.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Right turn = clockwise; left turn = anticlockwise. From North: right 90° = East, right 180° = South, right 270° = West.

NOTE

• Option 2 (South) would be reached after turning 180°.

• Option 3 (West) would be reached after turning 90° to the left (or 270° to the right).

• Option 4 (North) means no turn or a full 360° turn.

• Direction wheel (clockwise): N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW.

question: In the code "X ≤ Y > Z", which of the following is true?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Y > Z.

GIVEN

• Coded relation: X ≤ Y > Z (that is, X ≤ Y and Y > Z).

SOLUTION

• The first part says X is less than or equal to Y. The second part says Y is greater than Z.

• Y > Z is stated directly, so it is definitely true.

• X and Z are not linked through a common direction. X ≤ Y and Z < Y, so both are below Y, but their mutual comparison is not fixed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• A conclusion is valid only if the symbols form one chain in a single direction. In "X ≤ Y > Z" the arrow points to Y from both sides, so no relation between X and Z can be drawn; only the given Y > Z is certain.

NOTE

• Option 1 (X > Z) is not certain: X could be less than, equal to or greater than Z (both are below Y).

• Option 2 (X ≤ Z) is not certain for the same reason.

• Option 3 (X = Y) is not certain: the sign is "≤", which means X may be less than or equal to Y.

• Tip: in coded inequality questions, check for a common "peak" or "valley" element; if both ends point away from or towards the middle element, no relation between the end elements follows.

question: A man is facing east and walks 10 meters. He then turns left and walks 10 meters. In which direction is he now from his starting point?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. North.

GIVEN

• Facing East, walks 10 m; turns left; walks 10 m. Required: his direction from the starting point.

SOLUTION

• Facing East, a left turn makes him face North.

• Path: 10 m East, then 10 m North. Position relative to start: 10 m East and 10 m North.

• Strictly, such a position lies in the North-East direction (at 45°), about 10√2 ≈ 14.1 m from the start.

• The options do not include North-East. Among the given options, the PDF key is North, because the final movement was towards North (the last leg of the journey).

• (Flagged for verification: the exact direction from the starting point is North-East, but North-East is not given in the options.)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Draw the path: right arrow 10 units, then up arrow 10 units. The straight line from start to end goes diagonally up-right, i.e. North-East.

NOTE

• Option 2 (West) is wrong: he never moved towards West.

• Option 3 (South) is wrong: he never moved towards South.

• Option 4 (East) is wrong: although the first leg was East, the final displacement also has a 10 m northward component.

• Note: the answer follows the key printed in the PDF (Option 1). A purist answer would be North-East.

question: In a line, a boy is 25th from the left and 20th from the right. How many boys are there in the line?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 44.

GIVEN

• Position from the left = 25. Position from the right = 20.

SOLUTION

• Formula: Total = (position from left) + (position from right) − 1.

• Total = 25 + 20 − 1 = 44. (The boy is counted twice, once in each count, so one is subtracted.)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Add both positions and subtract 1: 25 + 20 = 45, 45 − 1 = 44.

NOTE

• Option 2 (45) forgets to subtract the boy who has been counted twice.

• Option 3 (46) wrongly adds 1.

• Option 4 (50) has no basis in the given positions.

• Check: boys to the left of him = 24; boys to his right = 19; plus himself = 24 + 19 + 1 = 44.

question: If 3 + 5 = 34, 2 + 4 = 20, then 6 + 7 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 85.

GIVEN

• 3 + 5 = 34 and 2 + 4 = 20. Required: 6 + 7.

SOLUTION

• Test the rule "sum of squares": 3² + 5² = 9 + 25 = 34 ✓ and 2² + 4² = 4 + 16 = 20 ✓.

• So the rule is a + b → a² + b².

• 6 + 7 → 6² + 7² = 36 + 49 = 85.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• When the answer is bigger than the sum or the product, think of squares: 34 = 9 + 25 and 20 = 4 + 16.

NOTE

• Option 1 (92): not equal to 36 + 49. ✗

• Option 3 (80): 80 = 6² + 44 does not fit the pattern. ✗

• Option 4 (88): not the sum of the squares of 6 and 7. ✗

• Other common rules: a² − b², (a + b)² − something, a × b + a + b.

question: In a coded laguage FINGERS are coded as NIFGSRE then find the code of GENERAL?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. negelar.

GIVEN

• FINGERS → NIFGSRE. Required: GENERAL.

SOLUTION

• FINGERS has 7 letters: F I N | G | E R S.

• Code: N I F | G | S R E, so the first three letters (FIN) are reversed to NIF, the middle letter (G) stays the same, and the last three letters (ERS) are reversed to SRE.

• GENERAL has 7 letters: G E N | E | R A L.

• Reverse the first three: GEN → NEG. The middle E stays. Reverse the last three: RAL → LAR.

• Code = NEG + E + LAR = NEGELAR (negelar).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Split the 7-letter word as 3 + 1 + 3 and reverse the two 3-letter blocks.

NOTE

• Option 2 (neeglar) is wrong: the first block would be NEE instead of NEG.

• Option 3 (neglear) is wrong: the blocks are not reversed correctly (ends with EAR instead of LAR).

• Option 4 (negealr) is wrong: the last block is ALR instead of LAR.

• Tip: for word-reversal coding, find which letters stay fixed and which blocks are reversed.

question: A company offers a product with many benefits but little evidence. What is a critical thinker's response?
option_2: Check reviews, data, and comparisons before deciding
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Check reviews, data, and comparisons before deciding.

GIVEN

• A product claims many benefits but there is little evidence to support them.

SOLUTION

• A critical thinker does not accept claims without proof. When evidence is weak, the right step is to verify: read independent reviews, look for data and compare with similar products before deciding.

• Therefore the best response is "Check reviews, data, and comparisons before deciding".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Pick the option that involves evidence, analysis and verification; reject options that rely on emotion, advertising or peer pressure.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Buy it immediately) is wrong: it accepts the claim without evidence.

• Option 3 (Believe the advertisement) is wrong: advertisements are biased towards selling the product.

• Option 4 (Follow what friends say) is wrong: opinions of friends are subjective and may not be based on evidence.

• Critical thinking = questioning claims, evaluating evidence and reaching reasoned decisions.

question: How many meaningful English words can be formed using any 4 letters of the word "PLAIN"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. More than 5.

GIVEN

• Word: PLAIN (letters P, L, A, I, N). Words of 4 letters are to be formed using any 4 of these letters.

SOLUTION

• Choose 4 letters from the 5 available and arrange them into real words.

• From P, L, A, I: PAIL, LAPI is not a word, but "PAIL" is valid.

• From P, A, I, N: PAIN, PINA (a pineapple fibre/cloth).

• From L, A, I, N: NAIL, LAIN, ANIL (the indigo plant).

• From P, L, A, N: PLAN.

• Meaningful words found: PAIL, PAIN, NAIL, LAIN, ANIL, PLAN, PINA, giving more than 5 words.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Just list quickly: PAIN, PAIL, PLAN, NAIL, LAIN, ANIL: already 6 common words, so the answer is "More than 5".

NOTE

• Option 1 (3), Option 2 (4) and Option 3 (5) are wrong: at least six meaningful words (PAIN, PAIL, PLAN, NAIL, LAIN, ANIL) can be formed.

• Tip: the count of words formed depends on the dictionary used; the question expects the learner to find that there are more than five.

question:
In these question, the statement is given followed by some inferences. You must consider the statement to be true even if it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts and then decide which inference can be drawn from the given statement.

Statement: Owner of the company is lay off their 20% employees

Inference:

I.  Company is facing Financial problem due to bad market condition

II.  The employees who are laid off were not better performance
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. either I or II follow.

GIVEN

• Statement: The owner of the company is laying off 20% of the employees.

• Inference I: The company is facing a financial problem due to bad market conditions. Inference II: The laid-off employees were not performing better.

SOLUTION

• The statement gives only the fact of a layoff; it does not give the reason.

• A layoff of 20% of the workforce may be due to a financial problem (Inference I) or due to poor performance of those employees (Inference II). Both are possible reasons, but neither is definitely stated.

• The two inferences are two alternative reasons for the same event, so they cannot both be proved, yet one of them is likely to be the cause. In this situation the answer is "either I or II follow".

• (Flagged for verification: a strict reading of "inference" could argue for "Neither", because the statement gives no reason at all. The PDF key, Option 3, is retained.)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• When two inferences give two different possible causes of the same event, and one of them must be the reason, the answer is "Either I or II".

NOTE

• Option 1 (Only I follows) is wrong: I is only one of the possible reasons; it is not certain.

• Option 2 (Only II follows) is wrong: II is also only a possibility.

• Option 4 (Neither I nor II follows) is the strict-logic alternative, but the key given in the PDF accepts that the two reasons are complementary possibilities.

• Tip: "either-or" is used when the inferences are complementary and no further information can choose between them.

question:
Statement: A survey shows increasing mental stress among corporate employees.

Judgement: What should companies do?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Provide mental wellness programs..

GIVEN

• Statement: A survey shows that mental stress among corporate employees is increasing. Question: what should companies do?

SOLUTION

• The problem is mental stress. The best judgement is the one that addresses this problem directly and in a lasting way.

• Providing mental wellness programs (counselling, stress management, workshops) tackles the cause of stress and helps all employees.

• Firing, salary increases and extra leaves do not directly address stress and may even add to it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• In "judgement" questions, select the option that is relevant to the problem, constructive and practical; avoid extreme or unrelated actions.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Fire underperformers) is wrong: it is a harsh step that may increase stress and has no link to employees' mental health.

• Option 2 (Increase salaries) is wrong: higher pay may be welcome but does not directly reduce stress.

• Option 4 (Give more leaves) is wrong: leaves give temporary relief but do not solve the root problem; it is not as direct as a wellness programme.

• Tip: choose the option that is most directly connected to the issue in the statement.

question: If ‘A is taller than B’ and ‘B is taller than C’, who is the shortest?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. C.

GIVEN

• A is taller than B. B is taller than C.

SOLUTION

• Arrange in descending order of height: A > B > C.

• The last person in the order is the shortest, so C is the shortest.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Write the chain A > B > C; the smallest is at the end.

NOTE

• Option 1 (A) is the tallest, not the shortest.

• Option 2 (B) is in the middle of the order.

• Option 4 (Can't say) is wrong: the two statements together fix the full order, so the answer can be given.

• Tip: transitive relations (A > B and B > C give A > C) are always valid.

question:
Statements:

1. Some teachers are writers.

2. All writers are philosophers.

Conclusions:

I. Some teachers are philosophers.

II. All philosophers are writers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Only conclusion I follows.

GIVEN

• Statement 1: Some teachers are writers (I-type). Statement 2: All writers are philosophers (A-type).

SOLUTION

• Venn diagram: "writers" lies completely inside "philosophers"; "teachers" overlaps "writers".

• Conclusion I (Some teachers are philosophers): the teachers who are writers are also philosophers (I + A → I). Follows.

• Conclusion II (All philosophers are writers): the statement says all writers are philosophers, not the reverse. The philosophers circle may be larger than the writers circle. Does not follow.

• So only Conclusion I follows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• I + A → I (valid). The converse of an A-type statement ("All writers are philosophers" → "All philosophers are writers") is never valid.

NOTE

• Option 2 (Only II follows) is wrong: II reverses the "All" statement, which is invalid.

• Option 3 (Both) is wrong because II does not follow.

• Option 4 (Neither) is wrong because I follows.

• Remember: "All A are B" gives only "Some B are A", never "All B are A".

question:
Statement.

Computer as a subject should mandatory in schools now days

Conclusion

1. Computer study is not so much important

2. Now days computer is very important to make life easy and advance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Only 2 follow.

GIVEN

• Statement: Computer as a subject should be mandatory in schools nowadays.

SOLUTION

• Conclusion 1 (Computer study is not so much important): the statement says computers should be compulsory, which means the subject is important. Conclusion 1 contradicts this. Does not follow.

• Conclusion 2 (Nowadays computer is very important to make life easy and advanced): this is the reason why the subject should be mandatory. Follows.

• Hence only Conclusion 2 follows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Check each conclusion for agreement with the tone of the statement: an idea that supports a strong recommendation follows; an idea that contradicts it does not.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Only 1 follows) is wrong: it contradicts the statement.

• Option 3 (Both follow) is wrong because Conclusion 1 does not follow.

• Option 4 (Neither follows) is wrong because Conclusion 2 follows.

• Tip: the statement recommends something because the subject is useful; the conclusion that states its usefulness is a valid conclusion.

question:
In each of the questions below are given some statements followed by few conclusions. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements disregarding commonly known facts.

Statements:

Some laptop are keyboard

All Keyboard are working

Conclusion:

I. Some working are keyboard.

II. Some laptop are Working.
option_3: Both conclusion I and II follow
option_4: Neither conclusion I and II follow
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Both conclusion I and II follow.

GIVEN

• Statement 1: Some laptop are keyboard (I-type). Statement 2: All keyboard are working (A-type).

SOLUTION

• Venn diagram: the "keyboard" circle is completely inside the "working" circle; the "laptop" circle cuts the "keyboard" circle.

• Conclusion I (Some working are keyboard): by conversion of "All keyboard are working", we get "Some working are keyboard". Follows.

• Conclusion II (Some laptop are working): I + A → I. Some laptop are keyboard, and all keyboard are working, so some laptop are working. Follows.

• Both conclusions follow.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Rules: I + A → I (gives II) and the conversion of A → I (gives I).

NOTE

• Option 1 (only I follows) is wrong because II also follows.

• Option 2 (Only II follows) is wrong because I also follows.

• Option 4 (Neither follows) is wrong because both follow.

• Tip: always check conversion (All X are Y → Some Y are X) first, then the combination of the two statements.

question:
Choose the correct letters to complete the word.

B_ _TLE so that it forms a meaningful English word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A, T.

GIVEN

• Word pattern: B _ _ T L E (two missing letters).

SOLUTION

• Try the options by inserting the letters in the blanks.

• Option 1 (A, T): B-A-T-T-L-E = BATTLE ✓ (a fight between armed forces).

• Option 2 (Q, T): BQTTLE is not a word. ✗

• Option 3 (R, T): BRTTLE is not a word. ✗

• Option 4 (K, R): BKRTLE is not a word. ✗

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Look at the ending "-TLE": words like BATTLE, BOTTLE, BEETLE, BRITTLE fit; with the given options only A, T makes BATTLE.

NOTE

• Option 2, Option 3 and Option 4 do not form a meaningful English word with the given letters.

• Other words of this pattern: BOTTLE (O, T), BEETLE (E, E), BRITTLE would need 7 letters.

• Tip: in missing-letter questions, check vowels first, then common letter pairs.

question: If A @ B means "A is added to the square of B", then what is the value of 5 @ 3?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 14.

GIVEN

• A @ B = A + B² (A is added to the square of B).

SOLUTION

• For 5 @ 3: A = 5 and B = 3.

• Square of B = 3² = 9.

• 5 @ 3 = 5 + 9 = 14.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Translate the words into symbols first: "A added to the square of B" = A + B².

NOTE

• Option 2 (25) comes from squaring A (5²) instead of B.

• Option 3 (5) only gives the value of A.

• Option 4 (9) only gives the square of B and forgets to add A.

• Tip: read the operation in the words carefully; "square of B" means B × B only.

question:
Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows.

 

Statement:  All pens are books.

All books are papers.

 

Conclusion:

I. All pens are papers.

II. All papers are pens.

Which conclusion(s) logically follow?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Only I follows.

GIVEN

• All pens are books (A). All books are papers (A).

SOLUTION

• Venn diagram: draw the circle "pens" inside "books", and "books" inside "papers" (three concentric circles).

• Conclusion I (All pens are papers): A + A → A. Since pens ⊂ books ⊂ papers, all pens are papers. Follows.

• Conclusion II (All papers are pens): papers is the biggest circle and pens the smallest, so this is the reverse of the relation. Does not follow.

• So only Conclusion I follows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• A + A → A (All A are B, All B are C → All A are C). The reverse (All C are A) never follows.

NOTE

• Option 2 (Only II follows) is wrong: it reverses the relation.

• Option 3 (Both) is wrong because Conclusion II does not follow.

• Option 4 (Neither) is wrong because Conclusion I follows.

• Remember: "All pens are papers" is valid, but "Some papers are pens" is also valid by conversion.

question:
Complete the analogy by picking the word that reflects the same relationship as the given pair.

JOURNEY : KNVQODZ :: TRAVELS : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. UQBUFKT.

GIVEN

• JOURNEY : KNVQODZ :: TRAVELS : ?

SOLUTION

• Compare JOURNEY with KNVQODZ letter by letter: J → K (+1), O → N (−1), U → V (+1), R → Q (−1), N → O (+1), E → D (−1), Y → Z (+1).

• The shifts alternate +1, −1, +1, −1, +1, −1, +1.

• Apply to TRAVELS: T + 1 = U, R − 1 = Q, A + 1 = B, V − 1 = U, E + 1 = F, L − 1 = K, S + 1 = T.

• The result is UQBUFKT.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Check only the first two letters: T + 1 = U and R − 1 = Q give "UQ…", which only Option 1 has.

NOTE

• Option 2 (UUBQFKT): the second letter U is T + 1 (R + 3), not R − 1.

• Option 3 (USBWFMT): the second letter S is R + 1, not R − 1.

• Option 4 (TQZUDKT): the first letter T has no shift, but it should be T + 1 = U.

• Tip: for alternate-shift codes, write +1, −1 above the letters and apply them in order.

question: Five persons P, Q, R, S, and T are sitting in a straight line facing north. Q sits immediate left of S. Only three persons sit between R and T. P sits immediate left of T. Who is sitting in the middle of the row?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. S.

GIVEN

• Five persons in a row facing North. Q is immediately left of S. Exactly three persons sit between R and T. P is immediately left of T.

SOLUTION

• Number the seats 1 to 5 from left to right (for persons facing North, left is the West side).

• Exactly three persons between R and T means R and T are at the two ends (seats 1 and 5).

• P sits immediately to the left of T. If T were in seat 1, no one could sit to its left, so T is in seat 5 and P is in seat 4, and R is in seat 1.

• The remaining seats 2 and 3 are for Q and S. Q is immediately left of S, so Q = seat 2 and S = seat 3.

• Arrangement: R, Q, S, P, T. The person in the middle (seat 3) is S.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• "Three between" in a row of five means they are at the extreme ends; then use the immediate-left clues to place the others.

NOTE

• Option 1 (T) sits at the right end (seat 5).

• Option 2 (P) sits in seat 4.

• Option 3 (Q) sits in seat 2.

• Tip: always draw five boxes and fill the fixed positions first.

question: Six people P, Q, R, S, T, and U are sitting in a straight line facing north. U sits fourth to the right of R. R is not sitting at an extreme end. T is the immediate neighbour of U and S. Q sits third to the left of S. Who is sitting immediately to the right of R?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. P.

GIVEN

• Six persons in a row facing North. U is fourth to the right of R. R is not at an extreme end. T is the immediate neighbour of both U and S. Q is third to the left of S.

SOLUTION

• Number the seats 1 to 6 from left to right.

• U is fourth to the right of R, so U = R + 4. R cannot be at an end. If R were in seat 1, U would be in seat 5, but R cannot be in seat 1. So R = seat 2 and U = seat 6.

• T is the neighbour of both U and S. U is at the right end (seat 6), so T = seat 5 and S = seat 4.

• Q sits third to the left of S: seat 4 − 3 = seat 1, so Q = seat 1.

• The remaining person, P, takes seat 3.

• Arrangement: Q, R, P, S, T, U. The person immediately to the right of R (seat 2) is the person in seat 3 = P.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• "Fourth to the right" in six seats with R not at the end forces R = seat 2 and U = seat 6. Everything else then follows directly.

NOTE

• Option 1 (T) sits in seat 5, not next to R.

• Option 2 (Q) sits in seat 1, to the left of R.

• Option 3 (S) sits in seat 4, two places to the right of R.

• Tip: when a clue says "not at an extreme end", test the possible positions to eliminate one of them.

question:
What is the next set of letters in the series?

MNO,JLN,GJM,DHL,?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. AFK.

GIVEN

• Series: MNO, JLN, GJM, DHL, ?

SOLUTION

• Take each position of the groups separately, using alphabet positions.

• First letters: M(13), J(10), G(7), D(4) → decreasing by 3 each time, so the next is 4 − 3 = 1 = A.

• Second letters: N(14), L(12), J(10), H(8) → decreasing by 2, so the next is 8 − 2 = 6 = F.

• Third letters: O(15), N(14), M(13), L(12) → decreasing by 1, so the next is 12 − 1 = 11 = K.

• The next set is AFK.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Write the three columns of numbers: (13, 10, 7, 4, 1), (14, 12, 10, 8, 6), (15, 14, 13, 12, 11) and convert back: A, F, K.

NOTE

• Option 2 (AGU): G (7) and U (21) break the −2 and −1 patterns.

• Option 3 (AIK): the second letter I (9) does not follow the −2 pattern (it should be 6).

• Option 4 (AGS): G (7) and S (19) do not follow the −2 and −1 patterns.

• Tip: for sets of letters, work column by column; each column usually has its own constant difference.

question: If '+' means '×', '-' means '÷', '×' means '-' and '÷' means '+', what is the value of (26 ÷ 10) + (14 - 7) × 18?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 54.

GIVEN

• + means ×; − means ÷; × means −; ÷ means +.

• Expression: (26 ÷ 10) + (14 − 7) × 18.

SOLUTION

• Replace each symbol by its real meaning: ÷ → +, + → ×, − → ÷, × → −.

• (26 ÷ 10) + (14 − 7) × 18 becomes (26 + 10) × (14 ÷ 7) − 18.

• Bracket 1: 26 + 10 = 36. Bracket 2: 14 ÷ 7 = 2.

• 36 × 2 − 18 = 72 − 18 = 54.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Make a quick table first: (÷ = +), (+ = ×), (− = ÷), (× = −). Convert every symbol before calculating.

NOTE

• Option 1 (72) is the value before subtracting 18 (36 × 2); it forgets the last operation.

• Option 2 (90) results from adding 18 instead of subtracting (72 + 18).

• Option 4 (48) does not follow from the substituted expression.

• Tip: convert all symbols at once, then apply BODMAS.

question: Which of the following is newly introduced in Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita?
option_1: Mob lynching as a specific offence
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mob lynching as a specific offence.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 (भारतीय न्याय संहिता) replaced the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and came into force on 1 July 2024.

 

• Mob lynching (murder by a group of five or more persons on the ground of race, caste, community, sex, place of birth, language, personal belief, etc.) is a specific offence for the first time under BNS Section 103(2), punishable with death or imprisonment for life.

 

• The BNS has 358 sections (the IPC had 511) and also adds new offences such as organised crime, terrorism, snatching, and acts endangering the sovereignty of India (Section 152, replacing the old sedition law).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The BNS is one of three new criminal laws: the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 replaced the CrPC, 1973, and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023 replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.

 

• The BNS also recognises community service as a form of punishment for petty offences and makes provision for gender neutrality in certain offences.

 

NOTE

 

• Blasphemy provision (Option 2) is wrong: the old IPC had provisions against insulting religious feelings (Sections 295A and 298 in IPC, continued in BNS), so blasphemy as such is not newly introduced.

 

• Triple talaq legality (Option 3) is wrong: instant triple talaq was made a punishable offence by the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019, not by the BNS.

 

• Manual scavenging (Option 4) is wrong: it is prohibited by the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013, not newly introduced in the BNS.

question: Which state has the highest number of national park in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Madhya Pradesh (मध्य प्रदेश) has the largest number of national parks in India (about 12), such as Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Pench, Satpura, Panna, Sanjay, Madhav, Van Vihar, Kuno and the Fossil national parks. It is therefore called the "Tiger State" of India.

 

• National parks are protected areas notified under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, with strict protection of wildlife and no human activities such as grazing or cultivation.

 

• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands (a Union Territory) have about 9 national parks, which is the highest among all states and UTs after Madhya Pradesh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has around 100+ national parks, covering about 1.3% of the geographical area of the country. The first national park of India is Jim Corbett National Park (Uttarakhand), established in 1936 as Hailey National Park.

 

• The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) is the nodal ministry; Project Tiger was launched in 1973.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 2) is wrong: it has around 5 national parks (such as Bandipur, Nagarhole, Bannerghatta, Kudremukh and Anshi).

 

• Andaman & Nicobar Islands (Option 3) is wrong: it has fewer national parks than Madhya Pradesh.

 

• Assam (Option 4) is wrong: it has around 7 national parks (including Kaziranga, Manas, Nameri, Orang and Dibru-Saikhowa), fewer than Madhya Pradesh.

 

• Note: the number of national parks changes as new parks are notified; the answer follows the PDF key (Option 1).

question: Which of the following statements accurately describes a key objective of the Major Atmospheric Cherenkov Experiment (MACE) Observatory in Hanle, Ladakh?
option_1: To  study visible light from stars.
option_3: To observe radio waves from space.
option_4: To measure cosmic microwave background radiation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is To detect high-energy gamma rays..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Major Atmospheric Cherenkov Experiment (MACE) is an imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescope at Hanle, Ladakh, at an altitude of about 4,300 m, which makes it the highest-altitude telescope of its type in the world. It was built by the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) with ECIL and was inaugurated in October 2024.

 

• Its aim is to detect very high-energy gamma rays (VHE gamma rays) from cosmic sources, such as supernova remnants, pulsars and active galactic nuclei, by capturing the faint blue Cherenkov light produced when these gamma rays hit the atmosphere. (उच्च ऊर्जा गामा किरणें)

 

• It has a large 21-metre diameter segmented reflector, one of the largest of its kind in the world.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hanle also hosts the Indian Astronomical Observatory of the Indian Institute of Astrophysics and the Hanle Dark Sky Reserve (declared in 2022), which is a protected site for astronomy because of dry, clear and dark skies.

 

• Cherenkov radiation is emitted when a charged particle travels through a medium faster than the speed of light in that medium.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (To study visible light from stars) is wrong: MACE detects gamma rays through the Cherenkov flash, not visible light from stars.

 

• Option 3 (To observe radio waves from space) is wrong: radio astronomy uses radio telescopes (for example the GMRT near Pune).

 

• Option 4 (To measure cosmic microwave background radiation) is wrong: CMB is measured by microwave detectors such as satellites (for example Planck), not by MACE.

question: Which Commonwealth Games edition saw India finish second in the overall medal tally?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2010 New Delhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India finished second in the overall medal tally at the 2010 Commonwealth Games, New Delhi (राष्ट्रमंडल खेल 2010), with 38 gold, 27 silver and 36 bronze medals (101 in total), behind Australia.

 

• This was India's best-ever performance at the Commonwealth Games and also the first time India hosted them in Delhi (3–14 October 2010).

 

• India's position in the other editions: 2002 Manchester (4th), 2006 Melbourne (4th), 2014 Glasgow (5th), 2018 Gold Coast (3rd), 2022 Birmingham (4th).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Commonwealth Games are held every four years, and the "Queen's Baton Relay" starts from Buckingham Palace. India hosted the Asian Games in 1951 and 1982 (New Delhi) as well.

 

• The 2026 Commonwealth Games are scheduled in Glasgow, Scotland.

 

NOTE

 

• 2002 Manchester (Option 1) is wrong: India finished fourth.

 

• 2006 Melbourne (Option 2) is wrong: India finished fourth.

 

• 2018 Gold Coast (Option 4) is wrong: India finished third with 26 gold medals.

question: The demand curve shows the relationship between:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Price and quantity of goods.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A demand curve (माँग वक्र) is a graph that shows the relationship between the price of a good and the quantity demanded of it, with other factors (income, tastes, prices of related goods) held constant (ceteris paribus).

 

• According to the law of demand, price and quantity demanded are inversely related: when the price rises, the quantity demanded falls, and vice versa. Hence the demand curve usually slopes downward from left to right.

 

• Movement along the curve is caused by a change in the good's own price (expansion or contraction of demand); a shift of the whole curve is caused by changes in other factors such as income, tastes or the prices of substitutes (increase or decrease in demand).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Exceptions to the law of demand: Giffen goods (e.g. inferior staple food), Veblen goods (luxury goods bought for status) and expectations of future price rises.

 

• Price elasticity of demand = percentage change in quantity demanded ÷ percentage change in price. The supply curve generally slopes upward, and market equilibrium occurs where the demand and supply curves intersect.

 

NOTE

 

• Price and budget constraints (Option 1) is wrong: the budget line (not the demand curve) represents the budget constraint in consumer theory.

 

• Income and expenditure (Option 2) is wrong: the relationship between income and quantity demanded is shown by the Engel curve (income–consumption relationship).

 

• Cost and profit (Option 4) is wrong: this belongs to the theory of the firm (cost curves and profit maximisation), not to the demand curve.

question: What is the rationale behind granting Maharatna status to certain Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)?
option_1: To limit their autonomy in financial decisions
option_2: To provide greater financial and operational autonomy
option_4: To bring them under state government control
solution_text:
The correct answer is To provide greater financial and operational autonomy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Maharatna scheme (महारत्न) was started by the Government of India in 2010 to empower the largest and most successful Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) to expand their operations and become global giants. Its rationale is to give them greater financial and operational autonomy.

 

• A Maharatna CPSE can make investments in a single project of up to Rs 5,000 crore (or up to 15% of its net worth, whichever is lower) without needing the government's approval. It can also set up joint ventures and subsidiaries and make overseas investments, within limits.

 

• Eligibility (as per the guidelines): Navratna status, listing on an Indian stock exchange with the minimum prescribed public shareholding, an average annual turnover of more than Rs 25,000 crore, net worth of more than Rs 15,000 crore and an average annual net profit of more than Rs 5,000 crore during the last three years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The categories of CPSEs are: Maharatna, Navratna, and Miniratna (Category I and II). The Navratna scheme started in 1997 and the Miniratna scheme in 1997 as well. The Navratna companies can invest up to Rs 1,000 crore without government approval.

 

• NTPC, ONGC, SAIL and Coal India were among the first Maharatna companies; the Department of Public Enterprises (Ministry of Finance) administers these schemes.

 

NOTE

 

• To limit their autonomy in financial decisions (Option 1) is wrong: the scheme does the opposite and increases autonomy.

 

• To privatize them quickly (Option 3) is wrong: the scheme is meant to strengthen the public enterprises, not to privatise them.

 

• To bring them under state government control (Option 4) is wrong: CPSEs are owned by the Central Government and the scheme does not transfer them to states.

question:
Consider the following statements:

Statement I: The 5th Five-year plan proposes the twin objectives of removing poverty and attaining self-reliance.

Statement II: The rolling plan was launched between the sixth and the seventh five-year plan.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
option_1: Both statements I and II are correct
option_2: Both statements I and II are incorrect
option_3: Statement I is correct, Statement II is incorrect
option_4: Statement I is incorrect, Statement II is correct
solution_text:
The correct answer is Statement I is correct, Statement II is incorrect.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I is correct: The Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974–79) put forward the twin objectives of removal of poverty (Garibi Hatao) and attainment of self-reliance. (गरीबी हटाओ और आत्मनिर्भरता)

 

• Statement II is incorrect: The Rolling Plan was introduced by the Janata Party government (1978) when the Fifth Plan was terminated a year early; it came between the Fifth and the Sixth Plan (1978–80), not between the sixth and the seventh. The Sixth Plan began in 1980 under the Congress government.

 

• The idea of a "rolling plan" is that the plan is revised every year and a new year is added each year (a continuing, flexible plan).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Plan sequence: 1st (1951–56, Harrod-Domar model), 2nd (1956–61, Mahalanobis model, heavy industry), 3rd (1961–66), Plan holidays (1966–69), 4th (1969–74), 5th (1974–79), Rolling Plan (1978–80), 6th (1980–85), 7th (1985–90), annual plans (1990–92), 8th (1992–97, LPG reforms).

 

• The Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog on 1 January 2015; the 12th Five-Year Plan (2012–17) was the last.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Both correct) is wrong because Statement II is incorrect.

 

• Option 2 (Both incorrect) is wrong because Statement I is correct.

 

• Option 4 (I incorrect, II correct) is wrong because it is the opposite of the facts.

question: Who is credited with bringing global recognition to Indian classical dance through Bharatanatyam and was honoured with the Padma Bhushan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rukmini Devi Arundale.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rukmini Devi Arundale (रुक्मिणी देवी अरुंडेल) (1904–1986) is credited with reviving and giving global recognition to Bharatanatyam by freeing the old temple dance (sadir / dasiattam) from social stigma. She founded Kalakshetra (Chennai, 1936) in Adyar.

 

• She was honoured with the Padma Bhushan in 1956 and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship; she also became the first woman to be nominated to the Rajya Sabha (1952).

 

• She also worked for animal welfare (the Animal Welfare Board of India, 1962, was set up through her efforts).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Classical dance forms of India recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Kathakali, Sattriya, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam (eight, and Chhau is sometimes counted as a ninth).

 

• Bharatanatyam belongs to Tamil Nadu and is performed in the "Natya Shastra" tradition (attributed to Bharata Muni).

 

NOTE

 

• Mallika Sarabhai (Option 1) is wrong: she is known as a dancer and activist (Darpana Academy); she is also a Padma Bhushan awardee (2010) but is not the person credited with reviving Bharatanatyam globally.

 

• Uday Shankar (Option 3) is wrong: he is known for modern Indian dance and ballet (Padma Vibhushan, 1971).

 

• Yamini Krishnamurthy (Option 4) is wrong as per the key: she is a great Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi dancer (Padma Shri 1968, Padma Bhushan 2001, Padma Vibhushan 2016), but the reviver credited with global recognition is Rukmini Devi Arundale. (Flagged: more than one dancer in the list holds a Padma Bhushan; the key follows the PDF.)

question: What are the two major components of the GII framework?
option_2: Knowledge Drivers and Innovation Impact Index
option_3: Innovation Input and Innovation Output Sub-Indices
option_4: Research Efficiency and Knowledge Commercialization Scores
solution_text:
The correct answer is Innovation Input and Innovation Output Sub-Indices.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Global Innovation Index (GII) framework has two major components: the Innovation Input Sub-Index and the Innovation Output Sub-Index. (नवाचार इनपुट और आउटपुट उप-सूचकांक)

 

• The Input Sub-Index has five pillars: institutions, human capital and research, infrastructure, market sophistication and business sophistication. The Output Sub-Index has two pillars: knowledge and technology outputs, and creative outputs.

 

• The overall GII score is the average of the two sub-indices; the Innovation Efficiency Ratio (output ÷ input) shows how well an economy converts innovation inputs into outputs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The GII is published by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), Geneva. It covers about 130 economies; Switzerland has long been at the top, and India ranked 39th in 2024 and 38th in 2025.

 

• A large number of indicators (around 80) are used to measure innovation performance.

 

NOTE

 

• Innovation Determinants and Performance Metrics (Option 1) is wrong: these are not the official components of the GII.

 

• Knowledge Drivers and Innovation Impact Index (Option 2) is wrong: not the framework's components.

 

• Research Efficiency and Knowledge Commercialization Scores (Option 4) is wrong: not official GII components (the efficiency ratio is only a derived measure).

question: Lavani is a traditional folk music form of which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lavani (लावणी) is a popular traditional folk song and dance form of Maharashtra. The word "lavani" comes from "lavanya" meaning beauty.

 

• It is performed to the beats of the dholki (a percussion instrument) and is known for powerful rhythm, quick movements and lyrics on social themes, love and politics. There are two types: Nirguni (spiritual) and Shringari (sensuous).

 

• Lavani is the main part of the Tamasha theatre tradition of Maharashtra.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other folk forms: Powada (ballad of Maharashtra), Bhavai (Gujarat), Ghoomar (Rajasthan), Bihu (Assam), Garba (Gujarat), Yakshagana (Karnataka), Jatra (West Bengal and Odisha), Baul (West Bengal).

 

• Maharashtra's famous classical-style folk musicians include Bharat Ratna Bhimsen Joshi (Hindustani vocal) and Lata Mangeshkar.

 

NOTE

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 1) is wrong: its folk forms include Karagattam, Oyilattam and Therukoothu.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 3) is wrong: its folk forms include Ghoomar, Kalbelia, Kathputli and Manganiyar.

 

• West Bengal (Option 4) is wrong: its folk forms include Baul, Jatra, Gambhira and Chhau (Purulia).

question: How many types of emergencies can be proclaimed by the President of India under the Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Three.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Constitution of India provides for three types of emergencies (आपातकाल): National Emergency (Article 352), President's Rule / State Emergency (Article 356) and Financial Emergency (Article 360).

 

• Article 352: proclaimed on the ground of war, external aggression or armed rebellion. Article 356: proclaimed on failure of the constitutional machinery in a state. Article 360: proclaimed when the financial stability or credit of India is threatened.

 

• Every proclamation must be approved by Parliament within one month (two months in the case of Articles 356 and 360).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The term "armed rebellion" replaced "internal disturbance" by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.

 

• A National Emergency has been declared three times (1962, 1971 and 1975). A Financial Emergency has never been declared so far.

 

NOTE

 

• Two (Option 1), Four (Option 3) and Five (Option 4) are wrong because the Constitution provides for exactly three types of emergency.

question: Which raga is traditionally performed in the early morning?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhairav.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Hindustani classical music, ragas are associated with a time of day (prahar). Raga Bhairav (राग भैरव) is traditionally performed in the early morning (first prahar of the day, around dawn).

 

• Bhairav is the base raga of the Bhairav thaat and has a serious, devotional mood.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other time associations: Yaman – early evening; Malkauns – late night (midnight); Darbari Kanada – late night; Todi – late morning; Bhimpalasi – afternoon.

 

NOTE

 

• Yaman (Option 2) is wrong: it is an evening raga.

 

• Malkauns (Option 3) is wrong: it is performed late at night.

 

• Darbari Kanada (Option 4) is wrong: it is performed late at night and is associated with Tansen at Akbar's court.

question: Which initiative was launched in 2025 to provide digital identities and simplify verification for Indian Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Udyam Assist Platform.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Udyam Assist Platform (UAP) was launched by the Ministry of MSME in January 2025 to bring informal micro enterprises into the formal fold by giving them an Udyam registration (digital identity) through assisting agencies, so that they can access credit and government schemes. (उद्यम असिस्ट प्लेटफॉर्म)

 

• The main Udyam Registration portal was launched on 1 July 2020 for online, paperless registration of MSMEs, replacing the earlier Udyog Aadhaar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• MSME classification (2020): Micro – investment up to Rs 1 crore and turnover up to Rs 5 crore; Small – up to Rs 10 crore and Rs 50 crore; Medium – up to Rs 50 crore and Rs 250 crore (revised limits applicable from April 2025: Micro Rs 2.5 crore/Rs 10 crore, Small Rs 25 crore/Rs 100 crore, Medium Rs 125 crore/Rs 500 crore, as announced in Budget 2025).

 

NOTE

 

• Udyam Registration Portal 2.0 (Option 1), MSME Digital Identity Mission (Option 3) and Udyam Verification and Facilitation Scheme (Option 4) are not the initiative launched in 2025 as per the PDF key. (Flagged: the PDF also shows Option 3 as a red, wrong selection.)

question: In national income accounting, depreciation is subtracted from which of the following measures?
solution_text:
The correct answer is GDP to get NDP.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Depreciation (मूल्यह्रास or consumption of fixed capital) is the loss in the value of capital goods through wear and tear. Net Domestic Product (NDP) = GDP − Depreciation.

 

• Similarly, NNP = GNP − Depreciation. Net measures therefore exclude depreciation.

 

• GNP = GDP + Net factor income from abroad (NFIA).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• NNP at factor cost = National Income = NNP at market prices − indirect taxes + subsidies.

 

• Personal income = National income − undistributed profits − corporate tax − social security contributions + transfer payments.

 

NOTE

 

• GNP to get GDP (Option 2) is wrong: GDP is obtained from GNP by subtracting net factor income from abroad, not depreciation.

 

• NNP to get GNP (Option 3) is wrong: depreciation is added to NNP to get GNP (reverse direction).

 

• Personal income (Option 4) is wrong: depreciation is not subtracted to obtain personal income.

question: Which Veda contains the earliest historical reference to the Dasarajna conflict?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rigveda.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Dasarajna (दाशराज्ञ) or "Battle of Ten Kings" is described in the Rigveda (Mandala 7, hymns attributed to Vasishtha). It was fought on the banks of the river Parushni (Ravi), in which the Bharata king Sudas defeated a confederation of ten tribes.

 

• The Rigveda is the oldest Veda and the earliest source for Early Vedic history.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Vedas: Rigveda (hymns), Samaveda (melodies), Yajurveda (sacrificial formulae), Atharvaveda (spells and charms). The Rigveda has 10 mandalas and 1028 hymns.

 

NOTE

 

• Atharvaveda (Option 1), Samaveda (Option 2) and Yajurveda (Option 4) are wrong because the Dasarajna battle is described in the Rigveda.

question: In a federal system resting on "limited government," the Supreme Court is designed to be the final authority for what specific purpose?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Constitutional Interpretation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a federal system with a written constitution and limited government, the Supreme Court is the guardian and final interpreter of the Constitution (संविधान की व्याख्या).

 

• It decides disputes between the Centre and states (Article 131), and through judicial review (Articles 13, 32, 131, 226) it can strike down laws that violate the Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 141: law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts in India. Article 143: advisory jurisdiction. Article 137: power of review.

 

NOTE

 

• Administrative Oversight (Option 1) is wrong: this is an executive function.

 

• Criminal Appeals (Option 3) is wrong: the Court hears them, but it is not the specific purpose for which it is final authority in a limited-government federation.

 

• Legislative Drafting (Option 4) is wrong: drafting laws is the work of the legislature and the executive.

question: According to Hugo de Vries, what is the primary cause of speciation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Large mutations.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hugo de Vries (Dutch botanist), working on the evening primrose (*Oenothera lamarckiana*), proposed the Mutation Theory (उत्परिवर्तन सिद्धांत) in 1901. According to it, new species arise suddenly through large, discontinuous mutations, not through small gradual variations.

 

• Such large mutations are called saltations, and they can produce a new species in a single step.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Darwin's theory of natural selection is based on small, continuous, gradual variations. De Vries, along with Correns and Tschermak, is also credited with rediscovering Mendel's work in 1900.

 

NOTE

 

• Gradual variations (Option 1) and Minor changes (Option 3) are wrong: these are the basis of Darwin's theory, which de Vries rejected as the main cause of speciation.

 

• Natural selection (Option 2) is wrong: this is Darwin and Wallace's mechanism, not de Vries's.

question: What type of stone was specifically chosen by sculptors of the Gandhara School for their high relief carvings?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Blue Schist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Gandhara School of Art (गांधार कला शैली) flourished from the 1st century BCE to about the 5th century CE under the Kushanas. Its sculptors mostly used blue-grey schist (also grey sandstone) and, later, stucco and clay.

 

• It shows Greco-Roman influence (Indo-Greek style) and is known for the Buddha shown in Hellenistic features (wavy hair, drapery).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Mathura School mainly used spotted red sandstone and was entirely indigenous. The Amaravati School used white marble (limestone).

 

NOTE

 

• Red sandstone (Option 1) is wrong: it is associated with the Mathura School.

 

• Black basalt (Option 3) is wrong: it is not the typical Gandhara stone.

 

• White marble (Option 4) is wrong: it is associated with the Amaravati School (marble/limestone).

question: Which is the brightest star visible in the night sky?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sirius.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sirius (व्याध / लुब्धक, the "Dog Star") in the constellation Canis Major is the brightest star in the night sky, with an apparent magnitude of about −1.46. It is about 8.6 light-years away.

 

• It is a binary system (Sirius A, a main-sequence star, and Sirius B, a white dwarf).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Brightness order: Sirius, Canopus, Alpha Centauri, Arcturus, Vega. The nearest star to the Sun is Proxima Centauri.

 

• The brightest object in the night sky overall is the Moon, followed by Venus among the planets.

 

NOTE

 

• Polaris (Option 1) is wrong: the Pole Star is of only moderate brightness, notable for marking north.

 

• Betelgeuse (Option 3) is wrong: it is a red supergiant in Orion and is much fainter than Sirius.

 

• Vega (Option 4) is wrong: it is bright but fainter than Sirius.

question: Which of the following best describes the Arabesque style used in Indo-Islamic buildings?
option_2: Decorative motifs of human figures and animals
solution_text:
The correct answer is Interlacing floral and vegetal designs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Arabesque is an Islamic decorative art form made of interlacing, rhythmic floral and vegetal (plant-based) scrolls and tendrils. It is widely seen in Indo-Islamic architecture (e.g. on arches and walls of tombs and mosques).

 

• Because Islamic art generally avoids depicting living beings in religious buildings, it uses plant-like and abstract patterns.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other elements of Indo-Islamic decoration: calligraphy (Arabic inscriptions, e.g. Quranic verses), geometric patterns (girih / star designs) and pietra dura (inlay work, e.g. the Taj Mahal).

 

NOTE

 

• Calligraphic inscriptions (Option 1) is wrong: that describes calligraphy, a separate element.

 

• Decorative motifs of human figures and animals (Option 2) is wrong: such figural motifs are generally avoided.

 

• Repeated geometric star-shaped designs (Option 4) is wrong: that describes geometric (girih) patterns, not arabesque.

question: Which Article provides for the establishment of an Inter-State Council?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 263.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 263 of the Constitution empowers the President to establish an Inter-State Council (अंतर-राज्य परिषद) if it appears that the public interest would be served, to investigate and discuss subjects of common interest between the states, or the Union and states.

 

• The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990 on the recommendation of the Sarkaria Commission; the Prime Minister is its chairman.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 262: disputes relating to inter-state rivers. Article 280: Finance Commission. Article 312: All-India Services. Article 307: Inter-State Trade and Commerce Commission.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 261 (Option 1) is wrong: it deals with public acts, records and judicial proceedings (full faith and credit).

 

• Article 267 (Option 3) is wrong: it provides for the Contingency Fund of India.

 

• Article 272 (Option 4) is wrong: it is the old article on the distribution of union excise duties (omitted by the 80th Amendment).

question: Before 1991, a system of licenses, quotas, and permits restricted private sector growth. What was this system called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is License Raj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The system of industrial licences, quotas and permits that regulated private enterprise in India before the 1991 reforms was called the License Raj (लाइसेंस राज), also called the Permit Raj.

 

• It was based on the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951, and the economy was heavily controlled by the state.

 

• It ended with the New Economic Policy of 1991 (LPG: Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation) introduced under PM P.V. Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Dr Manmohan Singh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The July 1991 reforms abolished industrial licensing for most industries, devalued the rupee and reduced import tariffs. The term "License Raj" was popularised by C. Rajagopalachari, who criticised it.

 

NOTE

 

• Quota System (Option 1), Permit Regime (Option 2) and Control Mechanism (Option 3) are wrong: these are generic descriptive terms, not the standard name "License Raj" used for this system.

question: Which novel by South Korean Nobel laureate Han Kang was awarded the 2026 National Book Critics Circle Award for Fiction?

NOTE

• Milkman (Option 3) is wrong: it is a 2018 novel by Anna Burns (Booker Prize 2018), not by Han Kang.

 

• Bliss Montage (Option 4) is wrong: it is a short-story collection by Ling Ma, not by Han Kang. (The PDF also shows Option 4 as a red, wrong selection.)

question: The widespread popularity of Francois Bernier’s writings in Europe, despite their acknowledged inaccuracies, most strongly reflects which underlying factor?
option_4: His writings were sole source on India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narratives reinforcing European comparisons accepted..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• François Bernier was a French physician and traveller who visited India during the Mughal period (1656–68) and wrote *Travels in the Mogul Empire*. He compared Mughal India with Europe, describing it as poorer and arguing that there was no private property in land (the Crown owned all land), which he held was the cause of its decline.

 

• His writings were popular in Europe, despite their inaccuracies, because they reinforced the comparisons and ideas about the East already accepted in Europe (the later idea of "Oriental despotism").

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other foreign travellers: Ibn Battuta (Tughlaq period), Al-Biruni (Mahmud of Ghazni), Tavernier and Manucci. Marx and others later used Bernier's views in the "Asiatic mode of production".

 

NOTE

 

• Audiences preferred strictly factual accounts (Option 2) is wrong: the text itself says his writings were inaccurate.

 

• Authority tied to colonial governance/control (Option 3) is wrong: Bernier travelled in the 17th century, before British colonial rule.

 

• His writings were the sole source on India (Option 4) is wrong: many other travellers (Tavernier, Manucci, Thevenot) also wrote about India.

question: A dessert consists of a cone having a radius of 3.5 cm and 12 cm high, topped by a hemispherical scoop also with a 3.5 cm radius. Determine the total volume of this dessert.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 243.83 cm³.

GIVEN

• Cone: r = 3.5 cm, h = 12 cm. Hemisphere: r = 3.5 cm. Use π = 22/7.

SOLUTION

• Volume of cone = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3) × (22/7) × 3.5 × 3.5 × 12 = (22/7) × 12.25 × 4 = 154 cm³.

• Volume of hemisphere = (2/3)πr³ = (2/3) × (22/7) × 3.5 × 3.5 × 3.5 = (2/3) × (22/7) × 42.875 ≈ 89.83 cm³.

• Total volume = 154 + 89.83 = 243.83 cm³.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Cone = (22/7) × 49 = 154 directly (since 12.25 × 4 = 49). Hemisphere ≈ 2/3 of 134.75 = 89.83.

NOTE

• Option 2 (678.89 cm³) is far too large; it comes from using the wrong radius or height.

• Option 3 (220.45 cm³) is wrong: it is not the sum of the correct volumes.

• Option 4 (324.57 cm³) is wrong: for example, using (4/3)πr³ for a full sphere gives a different total (154 + 179.67 = 333.67).

• Formulas: cone = (1/3)πr²h; hemisphere = (2/3)πr³.

question: A cylindrical water tank of height 1.5 m and diameter 1.4 m is completely filled. Determine the estimated water does it hold (in liters).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 2310 liters.

GIVEN

• Height h = 1.5 m, diameter = 1.4 m, so radius r = 0.7 m. 1 m³ = 1000 liters.

SOLUTION

• Volume = πr²h = (22/7) × 0.7 × 0.7 × 1.5 = 22 × 0.1 × 0.7 × 1.5 = 2.31 m³.

• In litres: 2.31 × 1000 = 2310 liters.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• (22/7) × 0.7 = 2.2, so volume = 2.2 × 0.7 × 1.5 = 2.31 m³ = 2310 L.

NOTE

• Option 1 (2200 liters) is wrong: it would come from rounding π × r² incorrectly.

• Option 2 (2400 liters) is wrong: it is not the volume for these dimensions. (The PDF also shows it as a red, wrong selection.)

• Option 3 (2150 liters) is wrong: it does not match the calculation.

• Remember the diameter must be halved before using the radius in the formula.

question: Find the length of the arc which is intercepted by a central angle of 90° in a circle of radius 14 cm. (Use π = 22/7)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 22 cm.

GIVEN

• Central angle θ = 90°, radius r = 14 cm, π = 22/7.

SOLUTION

• Arc length = (θ/360°) × 2πr = (90/360) × 2 × (22/7) × 14.

• = (1/4) × 2 × 22 × 2 = (1/4) × 88 = 22 cm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• A 90° arc is a quarter of the circumference; circumference = 2 × (22/7) × 14 = 88, so the arc = 88 ÷ 4 = 22.

NOTE

• Option 2 (23 cm), Option 3 (24 cm) and Option 4 (25 cm) are wrong: they do not match the arc length formula (θ/360°) × 2πr = 22 cm.

• Formula: arc length = (θ/360°) × 2πr.

question: If a solid metal sphere with a 4.2 cm radius is reshaped by melting into smaller spheres, each having a radius of 0.7 cm, what will be the total count of these smaller spheres?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 216.

GIVEN

• Big sphere radius R = 4.2 cm; small sphere radius r = 0.7 cm.

SOLUTION

• On melting, the total volume remains the same, so number of spheres n = (4/3)πR³ ÷ (4/3)πr³ = (R/r)³.

• R/r = 4.2 ÷ 0.7 = 6.

• n = 6³ = 216.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Number of small spheres = (ratio of radii)³. Ratio = 6 → 6 × 6 × 6 = 216.

NOTE

• Option 1 (450), Option 2 (200) and Option 4 (345) are wrong: none of them is a perfect cube of the radius ratio 6.

• Remember: when a solid is melted and recast, volume is conserved (not surface area).

question: If the height of a cylinder is reduced by 20% and radius increased by 25%, what is the percentage change in curved surface area? (Use approximation only)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No change.

GIVEN

• Height becomes 80% (0.8h); radius becomes 125% (1.25r). Curved surface area (CSA) = 2πrh.

SOLUTION

• New CSA = 2π × (1.25r) × (0.8h) = 2πrh × (1.25 × 0.8) = 2πrh × 1.

• So the new CSA equals the old CSA: there is no change.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Successive change method: −20% and +25% → 0.8 × 1.25 = 1. (Fractions: −1/5 and +1/4 → net change = 0.)

NOTE

• Option 1 (5% increase) comes from adding the percentages (−20 + 25 = 5), which is wrong because changes in a product multiply.

• Option 2 (4% decrease) is wrong: it does not match 0.8 × 1.25 = 1.

• Option 3 (10% increase) is wrong: it does not match the calculation.

• Formula: CSA of a cylinder = 2πrh. Net % change = x + y + xy/100 = 25 − 20 − 5 = 0.

question: Which of the following is equal to the decimal 7.8125?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 125/16.

GIVEN

• Decimal = 7.8125.

SOLUTION

• 7.8125 = 78125/10000. Dividing both by 625: 78125 ÷ 625 = 125 and 10000 ÷ 625 = 16.

• So 7.8125 = 125/16.

• Check: 125 ÷ 16 = 7.8125 ✓.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• 0.8125 = 13/16, so 7.8125 = 7 + 13/16 = (112 + 13)/16 = 125/16.

NOTE

• Option 1 (63/8) = 7.875. ✗

• Option 3 (113/14) ≈ 8.07. ✗

• Option 4 (105/13) ≈ 8.08. ✗

• Tip: learn 1/16 = 0.0625 so that 13/16 = 0.8125.

question: If 2.3̅6̅ means the digits 36 are repeating after 2., then the value in fraction form is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 78/33.

GIVEN

• 2.363636… (the digits 36 repeat).

SOLUTION

• Let x = 2.3636… Then 100x = 236.3636…

• Subtract: 99x = 236.3636… − 2.3636… = 234, so x = 234/99 = 26/11.

• Also 26/11 = 78/33 (multiplying numerator and denominator by 3). Hence 78/33 equals the value.

• Check: 78 ÷ 33 = 2.3636… ✓.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Pure recurring part: 0.36̅ = 36/99. So 2.3̅6̅ = 2 + 36/99 = (198 + 36)/99 = 234/99 = 26/11 = 78/33.

NOTE

• Option 1 (23/9) = 2.555… ✗

• Option 3 (26/11) is numerically equal to 78/33 (lowest terms) and so is also mathematically correct; the PDF key marks only Option 2 (78/33) and shows Option 3 in red. (Flagged: Options 2 and 3 are equal in value; the key follows the PDF.)

• Option 4 (118/45) = 2.6222… ✗

• Rule: for a pure recurring decimal, 0.ab̅ = ab/99.

question: A businessman lent Rs. 10,000 to two individuals, one loan earning simple interest and the other compound interest, both at the same annual rate. After 3 years, the difference between the compound interest and simple interest amounts is Rs. 25. After 2 years, this difference is Rs. 8. Determine the annual rate of interest.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 12.5%.

GIVEN

• Difference (CI − SI) after 3 years = 25 and after 2 years = 8 (as printed in the question). Rate = r% per annum.

SOLUTION

• For 2 years: CI − SI = P(r/100)². For 3 years: CI − SI = P(r/100)²(3 + r/100).

• Dividing: (3-year difference) ÷ (2-year difference) = 3 + r/100 = 25/8 = 3.125.

• So r/100 = 0.125, giving r = 12.5%.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Ratio of the two differences = 3 + r/100. Here 25 ÷ 8 = 3.125, so r/100 = 0.125 = 12.5%.

NOTE

• Option 1 (18.65%), Option 3 (13.42%) and Option 4 (17.26%) do not satisfy 3 + r/100 = 25/8.

• (Flagged: with P = Rs 10,000 and r = 12.5% the actual differences would be Rs 156.25 and Rs 488.28, not Rs 8 and Rs 25. The printed amounts are inconsistent with the principal, but the ratio method gives the key 12.5%, which matches the PDF.)

question: A food truck uses 250 kg of flour per month. In a new eco-friendly recipe, it reduces flour usage by 20%. How much flour is saved in one month?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 50.

GIVEN

• Monthly usage = 250 kg; reduction = 20%.

SOLUTION

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• 20% = 1/5, and 250 ÷ 5 = 50.

NOTE

• Note: 250 − 50 = 200 kg is the new usage, not the amount saved.
